question: Controlled: what does widening the phosphonate neighbourhood from 5 kb to 10 kb change?
method: Same 344 Pantoea ananatis genomes, same code, screen on in both, differing only in antismash_phosphonate_neighbourhood. BiG-SCAPE was then run on each set of regions with the pipeline flags and PYTHONHASHSEED=0.
reading: Widening the flank does not move this taxon's GCF structure at all - the same five families with the same membership - while putting 63% more genes inside the regions every gene-content metric reads. The cost is 9% more antiSMASH CPU (311.3 -> 339.5 CPU-min). It remains symmetric: the 2,030 genes gained include upstream flank the cluster does not contain, so this buys completeness at the price of context.
caveat: One taxon, and one dominated by a single 180-member family. A taxon with families separated by narrow margins could behave differently.
